metadata.title: Add partial support for second-order derivatives (for grid.h's input)

issue_payload.body: Hi, As discussed in issue https://github.com/NVlabs/tiny-cuda-nn/issues/58, a backward_backward functionality is needed. For now, I managed to add a partial support for second-order derivatives, **only** for `grid.h`, and **only** for `d(dL_dinput)_d(...)` . This satifies the need of backwarding nablas's gradients toward grid params and downstream modules' params. **edit: now support d(dL_dinput)_d(input)** ``` # NOTE: currently support: # ✓ d(dL_dinput)_d(dL_doutput) -> kernel_grid_backward_input_backward_dLdoutput # ✓ d(dL_dinput)_d(params) -> kernel_grid_backward_input_backward_grid # ✓ d(dL_dinput)_d(input) -> kernel_grid_backward_input_backward_input # x d(dL_dparam)_d(...) ``` I tried my best to follow the code style of your original project, and have done various tests to ensure that the code is running correctly. The changes are made as little as I can, and the compiling has passed with no errors. ## Code tests I provide three testing tools for the newly added `backward_backward_input` functionality: https://gist.github.com/ventusff/57f47588eaff5f8b77a382260e7da8a3 1. :heavy_check_mark: test_train(): train a toy SDF model with eikonal term. 2. :heavy_check_mark: grad_check(): check backward_backward **numerical correctness** via `torch.autograd.gradcheck`. 3. :heavy_check_mark: vis_graph(): visualize torch compute graph ## Toy model compute graph: toy_model: ```python class SDF(nn.Module): def __init__(self, hash=True, n_levels=12, log2_hashmap_size=15, base_resolution=16) -> None: super().__init__() self.encoder = tcnn.Encoding(3, { "otype": "HashGrid" if hash else "DenseGrid", "n_levels": n_levels, "n_features_per_level": 2, "log2_hashmap_size": log2_hashmap_size, "base_resolution": base_resolution, "per_level_scale": 1.5 }) self.decoder = nn.Sequential( nn.Linear(self.encoder.n_output_dims, 64), nn.ReLU(True), nn.Linear(64, 1) ) def forward(self, x): encoded = self.encoder(x).to(dtype=torch.float) sdf = self.decoder(encoded) return sdf def forward_with_nablas(self, x): with torch.enable_grad(): x = x.requires_grad_(True) sdf = self.forward(x) nablas = autograd.grad( sdf, x, torch.ones_like(sdf, device=x.device), create_graph=True, retain_graph=True, only_inputs=True)[0] return sdf, nablas ``` You can see that the gradients of `nablas` are backwared towards `grid_params` (needs `d(dL_dx)_dgrid)`) and `decoder.xxx` (needs `d(dL_dx)_d(dL_doutput)`) through `backwardBackward`. ![attached](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25529198/158918445-a9c77462-2d21-465c-b260-81515faf43d4.png) ## Theoretical derivation From gradients of `dL_dx`, to gradients of `dL_dgrid` and `dL_d(dL_doutput)`. ### **edit: add theoretical derivations of d(dy_dx)_dx** ~~1. Since I add a **virtual** function `backward_backward_input` in `object.h:DifferentiableObject`, I must put a dummy error function in `network.h:Network` and `encoding.h:Encoding` to pass compiling, which inherit from `DifferentiableObject`. Currently this funciton just throw a NotImplementedError. I hope this won't hurt any current mechanisms, and you can finish the remain support for backward_backward later to cancel this dummy function.~~

discussion_timeline.author: ventusff
discussion_timeline.body:
Hi @Tom94,
I've finished the following implementation and tests, and I think it's probably ready to merge now :smiley: 
- [x] update with your latest convention of code and data convention, including `MatrixView` and `xxx_impl`
- [x] as you suggested, I add an implementation of `d(dL_dx)_dx`, which requires: 
  - [x] an implementation of  `d(dy_dx)_dx`
  - [x] an overload of `pos_fract` for second-order derivatives, and second-order derivatives for `Smoothstep`
  - [x] an additional kernel `kernel_grid_backward_input_backward_input`
  - [x] bindings update and modules udpate
- [x] passed additional `gradcheck` and `gradgradcheck` for the newly added `d(dL_dx)_dx`'s calculation; check numerical correctness under both `Linear` interpolation and `Smoothstep` interpolation (the previous gist script for testing is also updated)

~~I will clean and upload theoretical derivations for `d(dy_dx)_dx` soon.~~ In the meantime you can review my changes :)
**Edit: theoretical derivations are updated in the top PR comment.**

issue_payload.body:
In some circumstances, the tiny-cuda-nn install location is read-only at runtime. For example, tiny-cuda-nn python bindings may be installed in a virtual environment that is specifically made read-only at runtime to avoid unexpected changes. In this case, tiny-cuda-nn fails to import as the cache directory cannot be created inside this read-only environment.

Allow users to redirect the cache directory to a location of their choice via a new function in `modules.py`

discussion_timeline.author: Tom94
discussion_timeline.body:
Thanks for the contribution!

I'd prefer if the configuration of the cache dir was a Python setter rather than an env var. Like this:

```python
def rtc_set_cache_dir(dir):
   if not os.path.isdir(dir):
       raise ValueError(f"RTC cache dir {dir} does not exist")
   _C.rtc_set_cache_dir(dir)
```

The current code could be guarded against import failure by

```python
try:
    _rtc_cache_dir = os.path.join(_rtc_dir, "cache")
    os.makedirs(_rtc_cache_dir, exist_ok=True)
    _C.rtc_set_cache_dir(_rtc_cache_dir)
except:
    pass
```

tcnn's JIT will work fine without a cache dir (simply re-compiling instead of loading from cache)

discussion_timeline.author: drewgilliam
discussion_timeline.body: @Tom94  - would it be possible to do both an env. var. and setter for maximum flexibility?  I figured the environment variable would already make sense to most users since it mimics packages like pip (`PIP_CACHE_DIR`) and torch (`TORCH_HOME`).

discussion_timeline.author: Tom94
discussion_timeline.body:
I'd much prefer exposing just the setter and then leaving it up to the application built on top of tcnn to implement an env var setting if desired.

Multiple reasons:
- Priority: if both were allowed, should the env var or the setter take priority? I can imagine situations where either would be preferable, meaning it would be good to put the decision into the hands of app developers.
- Complexity: the env var, as well as priority logic, would also have to be implemented in the C++ and CUDA APIs of tcnn, potentially needing downstream changes in existing apps that already follow the setter paradigm (like instant-ngp)
- Precedent: right now, tcnn isn't directly user-controllable via env vars at all. Instead opting to be configured entirely by the app built on top of it. I'm not sure it's good to start changing that.

discussion_timeline.author: drewgilliam
discussion_timeline.body: @Tom94 okie doke - I've revised as requested.  I took your concept a step further, letting the function create the cache directory if it doesn't exist and do a quick `tempfile` test to make sure the directory is writable.

discussion_timeline.author: Tom94
discussion_timeline.body:
Thank you! I think the tempfile check is great -- however could you remove the `makedirs` part again and replace it with an `isdir` check?

The PyTorch extension should be as thin a wrapper around tcnn as possible, not introducing behavior that the C++/CUDA API doesn't have. I.e., `makedirs`, if added, should be in `rtc_kernel.cu`... and I think it's too late for this change for backward compatibility reasons.

discussion_timeline.author: drewgilliam
discussion_timeline.body: done - `makedirs` replaced with `isdir`

discussion_timeline.author: Tom94
discussion_timeline.body: Thank you!
